gpt-6.1-sol.claim: Reasoning effort accepts low, medium (the default), high, xhigh, and max.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "Set reasoning.effort to low, medium (default), high, xhigh, or max." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The none and minimal reasoning efforts are not supported; callers that used none should start with low.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "The none and minimal reasoning efforts are not supported."; Quote: "GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol do not support none; use low instead." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: Tool calling requires the Responses API; Chat Completions supports requests without tools.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "Use the Responses API for tool calling. Chat Completions supports requests without tools." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: When reasoning effort is not none, remove temperature, top_p, and top_logprobs, and on Chat Completions also remove logprobs.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "When reasoning effort is not none, remove temperature, top_p, and top_logprobs. For Chat Completions, also remove logprobs.". Stated in the migration checklist that opens with setting model to gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, or gpt-6-luna. Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: When migrating from GPT-5.5 or earlier, replace prompt_cache_retention with prompt_cache_options.ttl set to 30m.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "When migrating from GPT-5.5 or earlier, replace prompt_cache_retention with prompt_cache_options.ttl set to "30m".". Same migration checklist as above. Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: When an application changes reasoning effort between responses, use configuration_update items in standard single-agent requests and keep request-level effort unchanged to preserve the cached prefix.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "If your application changes effort between responses, use configuration_update items in standard, single-agent requests. Keep request-level reasoning.effort unchanged to preserve the prompt prefix for caching.". Same migration checklist as above. Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The vendor positions it for complex coding, computer use, and professional work when near-Astra performance at a lower cost is wanted, and tells callers to compare it with Astra on their own tasks.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "Use GPT-6.1 Sol for complex coding, computer use, and professional work when you want near-Astra performance at a lower cost."; Quote: "Compare it with Astra on your tasks to assess the tradeoff between quality and cost." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: Callers already on gpt-6-sol are directed to the migration guidance before switching to GPT-6.1 Sol.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "If you already use gpt-6-sol, review the migration guidance before switching to GPT-6.1 Sol." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The models catalog lists it at 2 US dollars per million input tokens and 10 per million output tokens, one fifth of gpt-6-astra's listed 10 and 50.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "$2 / Input MTok"; Quote: "$10 / Output MTok"; Quote: "Near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost.". Astra's row on the same page lists $10 / Input MTok and $50 / Output MTok. The page states the prices, not a benchmark. Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The models catalog lists a 1.05M-token context window, 128K maximum output tokens, an April 30, 2026 knowledge cutoff, and Functions, Web search, File search, and Computer use tools, the same values as gpt-6-astra's row.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "Near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost.". Row values read from the saved models.txt lines following 'Model ID gpt-6.1-sol': Max output 128K tokens; Context window 1.05M; Knowledge cutoff Apr 30, 2026. Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The guide's prompting best practices address behavior observed with GPT-6 Astra, and the vendor says to evaluate them with the chosen model; none is stated as measured on GPT-6.1 Sol.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote: "They address behavior observed with GPT-6 Astra; evaluate them with your chosen model and workload." Verified 2026-10-01.

gpt-6.1-sol.claim: The guide's delegation prompt tells the model to parallelize work by delegating tasks to another agent whenever it could save time or improve quality.
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Quote withheld: it is an imperative addressed to an agent. Recorded and deliberately NOT adopted into any shared body: the catalog's agent-orchestration-primitives overrides it with the named-problem escalation gate, as for gpt-6-astra. Verified 2026-10-01.
